        </div>
        <div class="review-content">
          <p>
            This research review focuses on Carol Putnam's groundbreaking work on interaction forces in the golf swing. 
            Her research has been instrumental in understanding how interaction forces between body segments automatically 
            create the proximal-to-distal sequencing pattern observed in skilled golf swings.
          </p>
          <p>
            <strong>Key Research Focus:</strong> How interaction forces facilitate the transfer of energy from larger, 
            proximal segments to smaller, distal segments, creating the characteristic kinematic sequence that maximizes 
            clubhead speed.
          </p>
        </div>
      </article>

          <h3>Interaction Forces and Proximal-to-Distal Sequencing</h3>
          <p>
            One of the most important findings from Putnam's research is how interaction forces automatically create 
            the proximal-to-distal sequencing pattern. This work demonstrates that:
          </p>
          <ul>
            <li>Interaction forces between segments facilitate energy transfer from proximal to distal segments</li>
            <li>The sequencing pattern emerges naturally from the biomechanical interactions</li>
            <li>This mechanism is crucial for maximizing clubhead speed</li>
          </ul>
          <p>
            This research provides crucial insights into the biomechanical mechanisms underlying efficient golf swing 
            mechanics and has important implications for understanding how skilled athletes coordinate complex movements.
          </p>
        </div>
